_comment: Pre-registered hook-latency budget (road-to-credible-install Phase 1). Committed BEFORE the first optimization landed, per the roadmap's pre-registration discipline: the numbers below are the acceptance bar the precompile + single-process work is measured against, not a post-hoc fit. Consumed by the bench harness (scripts/bench_hook_latency) and its CI gate. Every budget carries an owner and a review date per the Phase-6 budget-ownership lint.

hardware_reference.ci: GitHub-hosted ubuntu-latest runner (the numbers the gate enforces)
hardware_reference.floor: 1 vCPU reference container (documented ceiling, not CI-enforced)

pre_tool_use_cap_derivation._comment: Why p95_ci is 175 and not the 150 registered on 2026-07-27. 150 was NOT bent around a red check — it was measured to sit INSIDE the legitimate distribution, which concern-activation-policy.md § Deriving a threshold names as a false-positive generator by construction: `a threshold inside the legitimate distribution`. The gate was flapping on IDENTICAL code, and the flap was already diagnosed in this tree by road-to-per-turn-hook-economy step 0.5 — it names three main runs at 151, 152 and 117 ms and concludes cross-runner variance after step 0.4 excluded the CLI wrapper (2 ms). What was missing was never the diagnosis; it was moving the cap.
pre_tool_use_cap_derivation.rule: concern-activation-policy.md § Deriving a threshold — the observed legitimate distribution's p99, plus headroom. With n=10 the p99 is the max, so the cap is max + ~11%.
pre_tool_use_cap_derivation.measured_failure_rate: 5 of 33 tests.yml runs on main (15%), 2026-08-16..18. Several of those runs carry a failure followed by a success for the same step, i.e. the standing workaround was re-running the job by hand.

observed_p95_ms_gated_cli_leg._comment: One value per run, pre_tool_use, the `via cli` leg the gate actually compares. Every one is legitimate code — the reds differ from the greens only in which runner drew the job.
observed_p95_ms_gated_cli_leg.spread: 115-157 ms, i.e. 42 ms of run-to-run variance on unchanged code — 28% of the new cap and 37% of the old one

pre_tool_use_cap_derivation.why_not_a_retry_or_best_of_n: A second bench on the same job would not help: the spread is between runner classes (p50 111-148 ms), not transient noise within one machine, so a slow runner measures slow twice. Retry logic is the escalation if 175 flaps, not the first move.
pre_tool_use_cap_derivation.revisit_if: A GREEN run measures pre_tool_use p95 above 160 ms. That is no longer runner variance — it is the cost itself growing, and it belongs to the owning roadmap (road-to-per-turn-hook-economy, D-2: the dispatcher's own payload read+parse, once per event) rather than to a third cap raise. Raising this number again without a measured distribution beside it is the config-bending this block exists to make visible.

per_turn_composite._comment: D-1 of road-to-per-turn-hook-economy: the slot budgets above gate per EVENT, and a single tool call fires both pre_tool_use and post_tool_use with their full concern chains. A ten-tool-call turn therefore pays twenty dispatcher cold starts plus the prompt and stop slots while every individual slot stays green — the number the user experiences has no row. This row is that number. Registered by step 4.1; the CEILING is step 4.2 and is the maintainer's, so the row ships observe-only and CANNOT fail a build. Definition before bar, deliberately: two people computing two different composites would both call the row green.
per_turn_composite._aggregation_note: Documentation of the code, not an input to it: the bench reads tool_calls from this file but hardcodes the p50 aggregation and re-implements the formula, so editing `aggregation` or `definition` changes nothing. Kept because a row whose meaning lives only in a TS file is unreadable here; corrected from silence to a stated non-binding after the R2 review flagged both keys as unread.
per_turn_composite._observe_only_note: While observe_only is true the bench PRINTS the composite on every run, including the CI gate run, and never fails on it. Setting p50_ci to a number and observe_only to false is the whole of step 4.2 — no code change is needed to arm it. Do not arm it from a single run: the composite sums four slot measurements and multiplies two of them by tool_calls, so it accumulates runner variance faster than any single slot (risk 5), which is why the same absolute-cap-plus-pathology-net posture the slots use applies here too.

regression_gate._comment: Pathology net only — the ABSOLUTE budgets above are the binding gate for wall-clock. The original 20% window was falsified by measured GitHub-runner variance: two CI runs of IDENTICAL code measured p95 77-89 ms and 92-103 ms (+23% run-to-run, 2026-07-27, runs 30303438480 / round-2 tests.yml). Same rationale as the regression_pct 200 override on the evaluator timing budgets: a tight creep rule on shared-runner wall-clock flaps; sizes/counts keep tight windows, timings get absolute caps.

honest_null_consequence: If the budget is missed after precompile + single-process + lazy I/O, hooks ship default-off with an explicit opt-in flag and the measured numbers published under a 'known cost' heading. A resident-dispatcher daemon is NOT improvised as a rescue (council 2026-07-26).
